prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control; boundary River Intake Pump Station/Raw Water Screen Channel to High Service Pump Header. Elements: River Intake Pump Station (Ironwood): auto start per demand/depth; lost permissive->alarm/stop; maintenance release after isolations verified. Raw Water Screen Channel sends Rake Torque Snapshot to Maintenance Planner. Coagulant Dosing Skid (Marigold) sends Alum Batch Ticket to Laboratory Technician; receives Jar Test Photograph Set from Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (Sparrow); holds last approved dose if quality data bad. North Filter Gallery (Cobalt) staggers washes, reports status before counted as capacity. South Filter Gallery sends Filter Run Exception Note to Chief Operator; breakthrough->offline. Backwash Recovery Tank; Chlorine Contact Basin; Clearwell Level Controller (low-level pump interlock; sends Clearwell Diver Entry Permit to Maintenance Planner, who verifies isolation before confined-space release). High Service Pump Header (Juniper): lead/lag; produces Pump Bearing Vibration Clip. North/South Distribution Pressure Stations (comm loss->last confirmed mode). SCADA Historian Server (Lantern): time-sync, audit; uses Sample Chain Slip. Actors: Chief Operator (directs emergency priorities; produces Backwash Solids Manifest; requires post-event review after cyber/alarm failure/emergency action); Duty Engineer (authorizes logged, bounded temporary workarounds; receives Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log from Chemical Supplier Driver before chlorine storage change; confirms temporary controls understood before wet commissioning); Laboratory Technician (sends Sample Chain Slip; no control access); Maintenance Planner (Quarry); Distribution Dispatcher (Falcon; sends Pressure Zone Handoff Card; informed of Juniper/pressure station failures affecting zones/fire-flow); Field crews; Residuals Hauler. Requirements: Chlorine Residual Alarm high priority; role-based accounts, MFA remote access, segmentation; alarm shelving time-limited; upsets advisory/controlled/critical. Backup power for intake, screen, contact basin, clearwell, Lantern, Juniper, control room; UPS bridges transfer; loss of normal+standby power = emergency, notify Chief Operator/Duty Engineer. Reliability: sensor-failure detection, redundant comms, backups. Commissioning sequenced, tests with conditions/acceptance/reviewer. Modes: Automatic; Manual; Local; Storm Intake Mode (higher debris, dose verification); Emergency.

New part:
S229: Functional testing shall verify that the River Intake Pump Station, Raw Water Screen Channel, North Filter Gallery, South Filter Gallery, and Coagulant Dosing Skid respond correctly to local and supervisory commands.
S230: During integrated testing, Juniper shall demonstrate stable pressure control through startup, lead-lag transfer, and controlled shutdown.
S231: The SCADA Historian Server shall be checked for correct time synchronization, tag naming, data retention, and retrieval of key commissioning trends.
S232: The Chlorine Contact Basin and Clearwell Level Controller shall be tested under representative level, flow, and residual control conditions before treated water is released for routine distribution.
S233: Storm Intake Mode shall be exercised in a planned drill that confirms operator prompts, intake constraints, and return-to-normal steps.
S234: A Chlorine Residual Alarm test shall verify annunciation, operator response guidance, acknowledgement behavior, and escalation to the appropriate duty staff.
S235: The Chief Operator shall coordinate training so that operators understand the control concept, normal sequencing, manual fallback methods, and alarm response expectations.
S236: Operator training shall include classroom review, simulator or dry-run practice where practical, field walkdowns, and supervised operation during early service.
S237: The Laboratory Technician shall be trained on sample timing, result entry, data review responsibilities, and communication of unusual water quality findings.
S238: The Maintenance Planner shall review commissioning defects, recurring nuisance alarms, calibration drift, and equipment access problems before preventive maintenance intervals are finalized.
S239: The Maintenance Planner shall use the clip to compare observed pump condition with planned inspection intervals and corrective work priorities.
S240: Feedback from maintenance work orders shall be reviewed with operations so that control changes do not mask equipment degradation or create avoidable field effort.
S241: Distribution readiness shall be declared only after pressure control, reservoir or clearwell constraints, communications, and emergency contact paths have been verified.
S242: Falcon shall confirm that distribution readiness messages are acknowledged before any planned change in pressure zone operating status.
S243: Before distribution readiness is declared, the South Distribution Pressure Station shall use the card to confirm zone status, valve lineup, and communication checks.
S244: The North Distribution Pressure Station shall be included in readiness checks for telemetry validity, pump permissives, local alarm indication, and operator communications.
S245: During commissioning of residuals handling, the Residuals Hauler shall use the Backwash Solids Manifest to confirm load identity, destination, and acceptance requirements.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
